runs.content: Saturday is the full-sweep day — skim every domain's overview/index page rather than deep-reading one, bias toward cross-domain connections over investigation ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-11, a quiet Friday), log.md shows a Finance clippings-sorter run (5 new Morningstar pieces, 10 new watchlist stocks: ASML, Synopsys, CRH, Magna, ResMed, Warner Music Group, Amcor, Brown-Forman, Hormel, Kimberly-Clark) and six new podcast-summarizer pages (CyberHack: The Conti Files, Odd Lots on bond yields, Dividend Talk EP305, Diary of a CEO x Ed Zitron, Prof G Markets on bond/inflation, Behind the Balance Sheet x Rich Pzena). Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections cleared the bar: (1) Two freshly-listened podcasts — Odd Lots and Prof G Markets, both on the recent Treasury-yield surge — land on exactly the same bond-market-stress story Finance's own Dalio Big Debt Cycle piece (source-dalio-bond-market-supply-demand-2026-08-28, 9 red-flag indicators) and the Bessent-stablecoin piece have been tracking since late August; the two podcasts already cross-link each other but neither links to either Finance source, and vice versa. (2) Rich Pzena's podcast recounts his firm underperforming the S&P by 60 percentage points during the 2000 dot-com bubble before a turnaround — a real, quantified historical precedent for the identical mania Michael Burry explicitly names as his own analogue (source-burry-trading-post-2026-06-12: 'a repeat of his 2000 playbook... while the market chased a different mania (dot-coms then; AI infrastructure now)') — relevant right now given Burry's own LULU position is currently in the underperform-and-hold phase Pzena's story shows resolving well. Neither page cites the other. A third candidate (ResMed's fresh watchlist entry — the market leader in sleep-apnea/CPAP devices — versus Health's own Nestor 'Breath' research on mouth-breathing/poor-sleep mechanisms) was considered but set aside as the weaker, more inferential of the three; the wiki's own ResMed entry only says 'digital-health M&A,' not sleep apnea specifically. No investigation idea cleared the bar today — nothing in the new Morningstar batch or podcast additions pointed at a concrete, actionable gap beyond what's already open. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-11.

Friday's rotation focus is Lightfin + Games + Cooking + Sports Betting + Work. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-10), log.md shows only one new entry: a routine Cooking recipe-recommender run (3 suggestions for week of 2026-09-14 — Nasi Goreng, a Fuku-style Nashville hot chicken sandwich, Wild Mushrooms on Toast — drawing on the same three chefs, Bourdain/Chang/Slater, already fully covered in the wiki). Checked raw/lightfin, raw/games, raw/sports-betting, and raw/work for any files newer than the last thinker output — none found; all four folders are unchanged since the prior Friday sweep on 2026-09-04. games/prototypes.md and sports-betting/markets.md remain the exact same unpopulated placeholder tables they've been since 2026-05-01. Read work/overview.md and work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026.md in full to check an apparent mismatch (overview.md names five debate perspectives — Schmidt/Otter/Lettink/Gouvernel/Turnbull — while memory's Domain Content Status only mentions three); this turned out to be a false lead, not a gap: LaRocque's own piece (Source 2) already synthesizes all five names within its 'Where the Debate Gets It Right' section, so nothing is actually missing. Also checked whether Deel — named twice in the Workday debate source page as 'the more interesting bet' for who disrupts HR software — has any Finance presence; it doesn't, but Deel is a private company with no public investment vehicle, so this doesn't clear the bar as a concrete, actionable idea. No investigation idea or cross-domain connection cleared the bar today. Nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution — GAW still has no Finance idea page, Eat a Peach still isn't in Books, the WDAY short-research gap is still open, and both Games/Sports Betting stub tables are still empty.
